transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-03 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Anika Shah, Liam O'Connor, Priya Menon (Northbridge)

Auto-summary: short scout call to understand platform fit and constraints, gather success criteria and next steps.

00:00 Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Carlos our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Anika (Northbridge): Hi thanks, doing good. We're trying to see if Redwood can run our inference workload — low latency for chat, but also large context for policy review.
00:15 Carlos (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda — understand your workload, context length, languages, tool-calling needs, and then go over Hosted/Dedicated/Private options and next steps. Does that sound OK?
00:24 Liam (Northbridge): Yep that's perfect. We have two main flows — customer chat (short turn-by-turn, tight latency) and longer document summarization for compliance (30–40k tokens).
00:36 Priya (Northbridge): And security: we need SOC2, EU data residency and KMS integration. Also interested in audit logs retention.
00:45 Maya: Good, thanks. Quick question on volumes — what QPS are you seeing for chat and what's peak?
00:52 Anika: Chat baseline is ~15 rps but on marketing days peek around 120 rps. Docs are async, maybe a few dozen jobs per hour but heavy token counts.
01:04 Carlos: OK. For the long docs you're describing, context lengths in the 30k–40k range point us to models with longer context support or splitting with robust KV cache. We support both — we have verified 32k models and experimental 64k variants.
01:20 Liam: Do you have open-model recommendations? We've been evaluating Llama3 variants, Mistral and some LLMX forks. Cost is a factor.
01:28 Carlos: For production we usually recommend 1) smaller 8-bit quantized variants for low-latency chat where cost matters, 2) p95 tail-latency sensitive flows run on Dedicated capacity with optimized kernels, and 3) 32k+ context models for doc flows. For open models: Llama3 70B ERT (example), Mistral Instruct, and some community 32k-context forks. Each has tradeoffs on hallucination and tool-calling reliability.
01:48 Anika: Tool-calling — we need the model to reliably call internal payment/account APIs with structured outputs. Does Redwood support function-calling / tool-calling patterns?
01:56 Carlos: Yes, we expose function-calling primitives. You can register deterministic schemas. On the runtime side we support streaming, function call soft vs hard modes, and you can attach validators in the pipeline. There are caveats with open models around consistency — we recommend a small wrapper model or post-processor for strict schema enforcement.
02:16 Priya: On-prem vs VPC — data residency is a hard requirement for some EU customers. What are the limits of Private deployments?
02:23 Maya: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane — either VPC-hosted in your cloud region or an on-prem package. We integrate with KMS/HSM for key management and provide audited access logs. There are more setup costs/time for Private vs Dedicated.
02:35 Anika: Do you have SLAs for Dedicated — latency SLOs?
02:39 Maya: Yes Dedicated has SLA-backed targets for throughput and latency tiers. We also offer burst capacity for seasonal unpredictable spikes.
02:47 Liam: How hard is it to switch from Hosted POC to Dedicated? Migration complexity?
02:52 Carlos: We design the API layer to be the same across modes — redirects, model pinning, and routing policies are managed centrally. Most customers do a Hosted POC and then move to Dedicated with a rollout — we help with canary and A/B testing.
03:06 Priya: Encryption at rest and in transit — do you use customer-managed keys?
03:11 Maya: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we support CMK via KMS/HSM. Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers.
03:20 Anika: For the long-doc summarization, we worry about token cost — any recommendation on batching / KV cache?
03:26 Carlos: Prefix KV caching is effective: if you have repeated context (like same doc headers) KV cache reduces per-token compute. Also intelligent batching for async jobs helps unit costs. We can recommend batching windows based on your latency SLOs.
03:40 Liam: Any rough numbers — latency and cost comparisons between Hosted and Dedicated?
03:44 Maya: Roughly, Hosted (shared) for chat with quantized models gives 60–120ms p95 on small payloads; Dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernels can get sub-50ms p95 in many cases. Cost depends on quantization and batching — we'll share a pricing matrix.
03:59 Anika: Multilingual support — we need good support for English, Spanish, French, German, and Portuguese. Also some RTL languages.
04:08 Carlos: Many open models have varying quality by language. We recommend running a small eval set across languages — Redwood Optimize can run cross-lingual evals and show quality vs token cost. For RTL we might need special tokenization checks.
04:22 Priya: For compliance we need an audit trail of model versions and prompt logging — is that available?
04:27 Maya: Console provides token-level traces, per-request metadata, model versions, and deploy history. You can set retention policies for logs.
04:34 Anika: Are there gotchas with function-calling and private deployment? Does network egress to tool endpoints create issues?
04:42 Carlos: For Private on-prem, tool calls run internal to your network — Redwood can be configured to route function calls to internal endpoints via connectors. For VPC we use private peering. We account for that in security reviews.
04:58 Liam: Who owns fine-tuning or RLHF if we need to fine-tune on internal docs?
05:03 Maya: Fine-tuning is possible — we support fine-tune workflows on Dedicated or Private. For Hosted we have some managed fine-tune options but for sensitive data we usually recommend Private.
05:12 Anika: Great. For benchmarking, can you run a realistic workload that mixes chat and large-document summarization so we can see tail latencies?
05:20 Carlos: Absolutely. We'll want a sample dataset and traffic profile. We'll spin up a Dedicated-equivalent bench with the models you want and produce a spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1k-tokens.
05:33 Maya: Action items and timeline — we'll send pricing by Friday, Carlos will schedule the benchmark, and Priya will share security docs. Any other asks?
05:42 Priya: Please include examples of audit log exports and SSO/SAML integration docs.
05:48 Maya: Will do.
05:52 Anika: Thanks, this was helpful. Looking forward to the benchmark.
05:56 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with proposed times for the deep-dive and the benchmark.
06:03 Meeting ends.
